summary: Raleigh County, WV tower on Wriston (formerly Bacon) Knob, built 1950-51 for the state Conservation Commission and removed about 1972; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: FFLOS says the tower was removed about 1972; the Forest Lookouts page marks it Removed without a date

events.note: Built in 1951 per FFLOS; a September 1950 newspaper item says a crew was already working on the new tower
Newspaper reported the tower and observer cabin completed and that it would be manned from October 15, the start of the fall fire season (a plan, not a later record of staffing)
Forestry Division of the Conservation Commission announced a complete overhaul of the tower (Raleigh Register item dated July 22, 1959)
Registered May 27, 2016 as US 1616, WV 23; nominated by Ronnie Scarbro

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the 1951 tower replaced an earlier one. A 1950 newspaper item describes a new tower in progress and lists the county's three other towers without one on Wriston Knob, so an earlier tower on this site is not confirmed.

The register names the West Virginia Conservation Commission; the Forest Lookouts page is headed West Virginia Division of Forestry; a 1959 item calls the commission's forestry unit the Forestry Division. These appear to be the same body under different names.

The 1951 article names the site for County Forest Protector E.N. Wriston of Scarbro; the register names Emory 'Pop' Wriston. Neither source says they are the same man, so the story does not assume it.

notes_for_editor: Brief record matches the FFLOS entry. The story says no source describes the site today. The 1951 staffing is a newspaper plan, not a confirmed record of operation. The 'replaced an earlier tower' claim is unconfirmed (see resolved_conflicts). The 1951 PDF by Robert Beanblossom on Pop Wriston did not extract text and was not used.
